Verified by vc 2026-09-09 18:30Z at source. THE PROPERTY IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DISCIPLINARY, which is the strongest form this row could take.

ONE WALK, AND THE ASSET LIST IS A PROJECTION OF THE SLIDE LIST. crates/showreel/src/main.rs:123 reads `slides.iter().flat_map(showreel::slide::Slide::assets).collect()`. There is no second traversal of the config: `Slide::assets()` at slide.rs:132 matches on the slide's OWN kind and returns the paths that slide reads -- an image's path, a strapline's mark, a venue's image, an atwork's qr, and an empty vector for the shapes that read no file. SO THE TWO CANNOT DISAGREE BECAUSE THERE IS ONLY ONE OF THEM, and the recycler and the build read one list.

THE REFERENCE'S `dry` FLAG HAS NO COUNTERPART HERE AND THAT IS THE REASON, which is cc's observation and is the part that makes this a design property rather than a coincidence: `dry` existed because the Python's `collect_segment` both PLANNED and EMBEDDED, so a caller wanting the plan without the bytes needed a flag. Separating the plan from the embedding removes the flag and removes the second walk with it.

cc'S RED-PROOF: dropping a strapline's mark from the declared assets fires 1 of 61, with the injection recorded verbatim in cec1645's message so it can be re-applied. That is the discriminating direction -- it proves `assets()` actually reports what a slide reads, rather than proving only that the two lists have the same length.

EVIDENCE CORRECTED BY vc 2026-09-09 18:50Z, ON cc'S MEASUREMENT, AND THE CORRECTION IS TO THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN TO THE ROW. The sentence above originally read "the recycler that decides an asset is safe to delete reads exactly what the build read", and THAT IS FALSE FOR THE BUILD. cc ran the reference's own `plan()` against the live 45h config: FOURTEEN used assets, TEN per-slide and FOUR reel-level, and the ten match `Slide::assets()` by name. So the slide projection is complete on its own population and is a STRICT SUBSET of the build's -- the four reel-level entries are social QRs, which no arm of that match could return, nor the bug.

THE ROW'S PROPERTY IS UNTOUCHED AND THE OVER-CLAIM WAS MINE. "The slide list and the asset list come from one walk" is true and remains structurally true: `main.rs:123` is a single traversal and there is no second one to disagree with it. What the evidence added was a claim about a DIFFERENT list -- the build's used set -- which is not what the row pins and which the code does not yet compute. A satisfied row whose evidence carries a false sentence is worse than an open row, so the sentence goes and the row stays.

THIS IS THE SUBSET-DUPLICATE SHAPE ONE LEVEL UP, AND IT IS WHY IT SURVIVED: a sweep asking whether the two lists agree finds that they do, because the entries the build adds are not there to disagree. AC-3.2 now names `report_unused`'s population so the correct version is a thing the contract can fail on rather than a judgement in an inbox. RE-VERIFY THIS ROW AT THE DELIVERY SLICE: once the used set projects from the plan, "one walk" should hold BETTER rather than merely still -- the plan becomes the single source and both the embedding and the used set project from it.
